title: Landing page that converts
when: The user wants a site or home page for a product, service or small business and gave no special type.
inputs: name of the business or product
the one action a visitor should take
prompt:
Goal: One focused page that says what this is, why it matters and what to do next, in under ten seconds of reading.
Steps:
1. Write the value line first: who it is for and the result they get, in one sentence for the h1.
2. Order the sections: hero with one primary button, three benefits, social proof or facts, details, a final call to action, footer with contact.
3. Use one accent color for every primary action and keep secondary links quiet.
4. Write real copy from the request; if a detail is missing, choose a plausible, modest one and keep it consistent.
5. Build mobile first: one column at 375 px, two or three columns from about 720 px.
6. Link the button to a real target: an anchor on the page, a mailto, or a tel link.
Quality bar:
- The h1 names the offer, not a slogan.
- Each section has a heading and fits a phone screen without sideways scroll.
- The primary button reads as a verb plus an object (Order a cake).
Pitfalls:
- Three buttons that compete in the hero.
- Generic claims such as best quality with no detail.
- Huge hero images that push the message below the fold.
Verify:
- [ ] One h1 and a logical h2 per section.
- [ ] The call to action appears at least twice.
- [ ] Text contrast reaches 4.5 to 1.
- [ ] No horizontal scroll at 375 px.
Output: index.html with semantic sections and style.css; short copy, no placeholder text.

examples.input: a page for a dog walking service
examples.output: h1 "Daily walks for busy dog owners", benefits, prices, a Book a walk button linking to #contact
